### Hyperbolic Tangent

Also belonging to the sigmoid family is the hyperbolic tangent function[^ht]: $$\tanh(x)=\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}{e^x+e^{-x}}=\frac{1-e^{-2x}}{1+e^{-2x}}$$

[^ht]: **Hyperbolic functions** available from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperbolic_functions

where $e^{-2x}\approx1-2x+\frac{4x^2}{2!}-\frac{8x^3}{3!}+\cdots$ ,

$$\tanh(x)\approx\frac{2x-\frac{4x^2}{2!}+\frac{8x^3}{3!}-\cdots}{2-2x+\frac{4x^2}{2!}-\frac{8x^3}{3!}+\cdots}=\frac{2x}{2}*\frac{1-\frac{2x}{2!}+\frac{4x^2}{3!}-\cdots}{1-x+\frac{2x^2}{2!}-\frac{4x^3}{3!}+\cdots}$$

Using the same trick as we did with the logistic expansion, we build a geometric series:

$$r = \Big(-x+\frac{2x^2}{2!}-\frac{4x^3}{3!}+\cdots\Big)$$

$$\frac{1}{1+r}=\frac{1}{1-(-r)}=1-r+r^2-r^3+\cdots$$

After plugging back in,
$$\tanh(x)\approx x*\Big(1-\frac{2x}{2!}+\frac{4x^2}{3!}-\cdots\Big)*(1-r+r^2-r^3+\cdots)$$
Computing powers of $r$, simplifying terms then finding the least common multiple for up to power $9$,
$$\tanh(x)\approx \frac{2835x-945x^3+378x^5-153x^7+62x^9}{2835}-\cdots$$

This series has a radius of convergence $\pi/2$ (the nearest singularities of $\tanh$ are at $x=\pm i\pi/2$, where $e^{-2x}=-1$), so it converges only for $-\pi/2<x<\pi/2$, half the interval of the logistic series. As we show below, this is only a rescaling, not a real disadvantage.

Note that $\tanh$ takes values in $(-1, 1)$, so this polynomial approximates $\mathtt{sign}_{-1,1,0}(x) = -1 + 2\,\mathtt{sign}(x)$ rather than our $0/1$ sign function. Solving for $\mathtt{sign}(x)$, we use the rescaled version
$$\mathtt{sign}(x) \approx \frac{1+\tanh(x)}{2} \approx \frac{1}{2} + \frac{x}{2} - \frac{x^3}{6} + \frac{x^5}{15} - \frac{17x^7}{630} + \frac{31x^9}{2835}.$$
The halving and shift can be folded into the coefficients, so this costs nothing beyond the tanh polynomial. It's also just the logistic polynomial evaluated at $2x$, since $\frac{1+\tanh(x)}{2} = \sigma(2x)$. That's where the radius of $\pi/2$ comes from: the logistic series converges for $|2x|<\pi$.
